sanskrit: nṛsiṃhaṃ narayuktena paramālaṃkṛtena tam avahan yānamukhyena saha mādryā susaṃvṛtam
english: They bore that lion among men, well-covered, together with Mādrī, on the finest of vehicles, drawn by horses and supremely adorned.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa cāmaravyajanena ca sarvavāditranādaiś ca samalaṃcakrire tataḥ
english: They then honored him with a white royal parasol, with fans of chowrie, and with the sound of all manner of musical instruments.

sanskrit: ratnāni cāpy upādāya bahūni śataśo narāḥ pradaduḥ kāṅkṣamāṇebhyaḥ pāṇḍos tatraurdhvadehikam
english: Men, taking up gems by the hundreds, distributed there the post-mortem offerings of Pāṇḍu to all who desired them.

sanskrit: atha chatrāṇi śubhrāṇi pāṇḍurāṇi bṛhanti ca ājahruḥ kauravasyārthe vāsāṃsi rucirāṇi ca
english: Then they brought white, bright, and large parasols for the sake of the Kaurava, as well as beautiful garments.

sanskrit: yājakaiḥ śuklavāsobhir hūyamānā hutāśanāḥ agacchann agratas tasya dīpyamānāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: Sacrificial fires, blazing and well-adorned, tended by officiating priests clad in white, went before him while oblations were poured.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś caiva sahasraśaḥ rudantaḥ śokasaṃtaptā anujagmur narādhipam
english: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras by the thousands, weeping and burning with grief, followed the lord of men.

sanskrit: ayam asmān apāhāya duḥkhe cādhāya śāśvate kṛtvānāthān paro nāthaḥ kva yāsyati narādhipaḥ
english: "This lord of men, our greatest protector, having abandoned us and cast us into perpetual sorrow, having left us without a guardian — where will he go?"

sanskrit: krośantaḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sarve bhīṣmo vidura eva ca ramaṇīye vanoddeśe gaṅgātīre same śubhe
english: All the Pāṇḍavas, Bhīṣma, and Vidura, weeping aloud, came to a charming spot in the forest, on the even, auspicious bank of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: nyāsayām āsur atha tāṃ śibikāṃ satyavādinaḥ sabhāryasya nṛsiṃhasya pāṇḍor akliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
english: Those truth-speaking men then set down that palanquin bearing the lion among men, Pāṇḍu of untiring deeds, together with his wife.

sanskrit: tatas tasya śarīraṃ tat sarvagandhaniṣevitam śucikālīyakādigdhaṃ mukhyasnānādhivāsitam paryaṣiñcaj jalenāśu śātakumbhamayair ghaṭaiḥ
english: Then they quickly sprinkled his body — which had been treated with all fragrances, anointed with pure kālīyaka paste and the like, and consecrated with the finest ritual bath — with water from golden vessels.

sanskrit: candanena ca mukhyena śuklena samalepayan kālāguruvimiśreṇa tathā tuṅgarasena ca
english: They anointed him with the finest white sandalwood paste, mixed with black aloe-wood and with tuṅgarasa.

sanskrit: athainaṃ deśajaiḥ śuklair vāsobhiḥ samayojayan ācchannaḥ sa tu vāsobhir jīvann iva nararṣabhaḥ śuśubhe puruṣavyāghro mahārhaśayanocitaḥ
english: Then they dressed him in pure white garments of local fabric; covered in robes, that bull among men — that tiger among men, accustomed to the most precious of beds — shone as though still alive.

sanskrit: yājakair abhyanujñātaṃ pretakarmaṇi niṣṭhitaiḥ ghṛtāvasiktaṃ rājānaṃ saha mādryā svalaṃkṛtam
english: Authorised by the officiating priests who had completed the funerary rites, they prepared the king — well-adorned and sprinkled with clarified butter — together with Mādrī.

sanskrit: tuṅgapadmakamiśreṇa candanena sugandhinā anyaiś ca vividhair gandhair analpaiḥ samadāhayan
english: They cremated them with fragrant sandalwood mixed with tuṅga and padmaka, and with many other various perfumes in great abundance.

sanskrit: tatas tayoḥ śarīre te dṛṣṭvā mohavaśaṃ gatā hāhā putreti kausalyā papāta sahasā bhuvi
english: Then, seeing those two bodies, Kausalyā was overwhelmed with bewilderment and fell suddenly to the earth, crying "Ah! my son!"

sanskrit: tāṃ prekṣya patitām ārtāṃ paurajānapado janaḥ ruroda sasvanaṃ sarvo rājabhaktyā kṛpānvitaḥ
english: Seeing her fallen and afflicted, all the people of the city and the countryside wept aloud, filled with compassion and devotion to the king.

sanskrit: klāntānīvārtanādena sarvāṇi ca vicukruśuḥ mānuṣaiḥ saha bhūtāni tiryagyonigatāny api
english: All creatures, even those born in the animal kingdom, cried out together with the humans, as though wearied by the clamor of distress.

sanskrit: tathā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo viduraś ca mahāmatiḥ sarvaśaḥ kauravāś caiva prāṇadan bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ
english: So too did Bhīṣma son of Śaṃtanu, the great-minded Vidura, and all the Kauravas weep, deeply overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmo 'tha viduro rājā ca saha bandhubhiḥ udakaṃ cakrire tasya sarvāś ca kuruyoṣitaḥ
english: Then Bhīṣma, Vidura, the king along with his kinsmen, and all the women of the Kuru clan performed the water-libation rite for him.

sanskrit: kṛtodakāṃs tān ādāya pāṇḍavāñ śokakarśitān sarvāḥ prakṛtayo rājañ śocantyaḥ paryavārayan
english: O king, taking those Pāṇḍavas who had performed the water rites and were emaciated with grief, all the subjects surrounded them, themselves lamenting.

sanskrit: yathaiva pāṇḍavā bhūmau suṣupuḥ saha bāndhavaiḥ tathaiva nāgarā rājañ śiśyire brāhmaṇādayaḥ
english: Just as the Pāṇḍavas lay down on the ground together with their kinsmen, so too did the citizens — brāhmaṇas and others — lie down in the same way, O king.

sanskrit: tad anānandam asvastham ākumāram ahṛṣṭavat babhūva pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ nagaraṃ dvādaśa kṣapāḥ
english: Together with the Pāṇḍavas, the city remained joyless, uneasy, downcast even to its children, and desolate for twelve nights.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kṣattā ca rājā ca bhīṣmaś ca saha bandhubhiḥ daduḥ śrāddhaṃ tadā pāṇḍoḥ svadhāmṛtamayaṃ tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Kṣattā (Vidura), the king, and Bhīṣma, together with their kinsmen, performed the śrāddha rite for Pāṇḍu, replete with the nectar of the ancestral offering.

sanskrit: kurūṃś ca vipramukhyāṃś ca bhojayitvā sahasraśaḥ ratnaughān dvijamukhyebhyo dattvā grāmavarān api
english: They fed the Kurus and the foremost brāhmaṇas by the thousands, and gave floods of gems to the chief twice-born, as well as choice villages.

sanskrit: kṛtaśaucāṃs tatas tāṃs tu pāṇḍavān bharatarṣabhān ādāya viviśuḥ paurāḥ puraṃ vāraṇasāhvayam
english: Then, after the purification rites were completed, the citizens took those Pāṇḍavas — the bulls of the Bharata line — and returned to the city named after the elephant.

sanskrit: satataṃ smānvatapyanta tam eva bharatarṣabham paurajānapadāḥ sarve mṛtaṃ svam iva bāndhavam
english: All the people of the city and countryside continually mourned that bull of the Bharata line as though he were their own dead kinsman.

sanskrit: śrāddhāvasāne tu tadā dṛṣṭvā taṃ duḥkhitaṃ janam saṃmūḍhāṃ duḥkhaśokārtāṃ vyāso mātaram abravīt
english: At the conclusion of the śrāddha, seeing the people so afflicted, bewildered, tormented by pain and grief, Vyāsa spoke to his mother.

sanskrit: atikrāntasukhāḥ kālāḥ pratyupasthitadāruṇāḥ śvaḥ śvaḥ pāpīyadivasāḥ pṛthivī gatayauvanā
english: "The times of happiness have passed away; dreadful times have arrived. Day by day the days grow worse; the earth has lost its youth.

sanskrit: bahumāyāsamākīrṇo nānādoṣasamākulaḥ luptadharmakriyācāro ghoraḥ kālo bhaviṣyati
english: A terrible age is coming, filled with many deceits, overwhelmed with manifold faults, its righteous practices and customs vanished.

sanskrit: gaccha tvaṃ tyāgam āsthāya yuktā vasa tapovane mā drakṣyasi kulasyāsya ghoraṃ saṃkṣayam ātmanaḥ
english: Go, take to renunciation, and dwell composed in the forest of austerity — you will not then behold the terrible destruction of this lineage with your own eyes."

sanskrit: tatheti samanujñāya sā praviśyābravīt snuṣām ambike tava putrasya durnayāt kila bhāratāḥ sānubandhā vinaṅkṣyanti pautrāś caiveti naḥ śrutam
english: She agreed with "So be it," then went in and spoke to her daughter-in-law: "O Ambikā, we have heard that on account of your son's misrule the Bhāratas along with their dependants — and even the grandchildren — will perish."

sanskrit: tat kausalyām imām ārtāṃ putraśokābhipīḍitām vanam ādāya bhadraṃ te gacchāvo yadi manyase
english: "Therefore, taking this afflicted Kausalyā who is tormented by grief for her son, we two will go to the forest — if you agree. May it be well with you."

sanskrit: tathety ukte ambikayā bhīṣmam āmantrya suvratā vanaṃ yayau satyavatī snuṣābhyāṃ saha bhārata
english: When Ambikā said "So be it," Satyavatī of noble vows took leave of Bhīṣma and went to the forest together with her two daughters-in-law, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tāḥ sughoraṃ tapaḥ kṛtvā devyo bharatasattama dehaṃ tyaktvā mahārāja gatim iṣṭāṃ yayus tadā
english: Those divine women performed exceedingly severe austerities, O best of the Bharatas, and then, O great king, casting off their bodies, attained the desired state.

sanskrit: avāpnuvanta vedoktān saṃskārān pāṇḍavās tadā avardhanta ca bhogāṃs te bhuñjānāḥ pitṛveśmani
english: The Pāṇḍavas then received the sacraments ordained in the Vedas and grew up enjoying their pleasures in their father's house.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭraiś ca sahitāḥ krīḍantaḥ pitṛveśmani bālakrīḍāsu sarvāsu viśiṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavābhavan
english: Playing together with the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in their father's house, the Pāṇḍavas proved superior in all childish games.

sanskrit: jave lakṣyābhiharaṇe bhojye pāṃsuvikarṣaṇe dhārtarāṣṭrān bhīmasenaḥ sarvān sa parimardati
english: In speed, in hitting targets, in eating, and in rolling in the dust, Bhīmasena overpowered all the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: harṣād etān krīḍamānān gṛhya kākanilīyane śiraḥsu ca nigṛhyainān yodhayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: With great delight that Pāṇḍava would seize them as they played, in the game of hide-and-seek, and holding them by their heads he would force them to fight.

sanskrit: śatam ekottaraṃ teṣāṃ kumārāṇāṃ mahaujasām eka eva vimṛdnāti nātikṛcchrād vṛkodaraḥ
english: Vṛkodara alone would crush all one hundred and one of those princes of great energy without very much difficulty.

sanskrit: pādeṣu ca nigṛhyainān vinihatya balād balī cakarṣa krośato bhūmau ghṛṣṭajānuśirokṣikān
english: That powerful one would seize them by the feet, beat them down by force, and drag them screaming along the ground until their knees, heads, and eyes were scraped raw.

sanskrit: daśa bālāñ jale krīḍan bhujābhyāṃ parigṛhya saḥ āste sma salile magnaḥ pramṛtāṃś ca vimuñcati
english: While playing in the water he would clasp ten boys in his arms at once, remain submerged, and release them only when they were nearly dead.

sanskrit: phalāni vṛkṣam āruhya pracinvanti ca te yadā tadā pādaprahāreṇa bhīmaḥ kampayate drumam
english: Whenever they climbed a tree to gather fruit, Bhīma would shake the tree with a kick of his foot.

sanskrit: prahāravegābhihatād drumād vyāghūrṇitās tataḥ saphalāḥ prapatanti sma drutaṃ srastāḥ kumārakāḥ
english: Struck by the force of the blow, the tree would whirl around, and the boys would quickly tumble down from it together with the fruit, falling loose.

sanskrit: na te niyuddhe na jave na yogyāsu kadā cana kumārā uttaraṃ cakruḥ spardhamānā vṛkodaram
english: In wrestling, in speed, or in any exercise, those princes who competed with Vṛkodara never once got the better of him.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ spardhamāno vṛkodaraḥ apriye 'tiṣṭhad atyantaṃ bālyān na drohacetasā
english: Though Vṛkodara thus continually competed with the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and kept them in a state of misery, it was entirely out of boyish spirit and not from any treacherous intent.

sanskrit: tato balam atikhyātaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraḥ pratāpavān bhīmasenasya taj jñātvā duṣṭabhāvam adarśayat
english: Then the mighty-spirited son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, knowing Bhīmasena's exceedingly renowned strength, revealed his wicked disposition.

sanskrit: tasya dharmād apetasya pāpāni paripaśyataḥ mohād aiśvaryalobhāc ca pāpā matir ajāyata
english: In that one who had strayed from righteousness, surveying all manner of sins, a wicked mind arose out of delusion and greed for lordship.

sanskrit: ayaṃ balavatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kuntīputro vṛkodaraḥ madhyamaḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ nikṛtyā saṃnihanyatām
english: "This Vṛkodara, son of Kuntī, the middle of the Pāṇḍu-sons, the foremost among the mighty — let him be slain by treachery."

sanskrit: atha tasmād avarajaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ caiva yudhiṣṭhiram prasahya bandhane baddhvā praśāsiṣye vasuṃdharām
english: "And then, having forcibly bound the younger and the eldest — Yudhiṣṭhira — in chains, I shall rule the earth."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa niścayaṃ pāpaḥ kṛtvā duryodhanas tadā nityam evāntaraprekṣī bhīmasyāsīn mahātmanaḥ
english: Having thus resolved upon this wicked plan, Duryodhana from that time constantly watched for an opportunity against the great-souled Bhīma.

sanskrit: tato jalavihārārthaṃ kārayām āsa bhārata celakambalaveśmāni vicitrāṇi mahānti ca
english: Then he had built large and variously adorned tents and pavilions of cloth and blankets for the purpose of water-sports, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pramāṇakoṭyām uddeśaṃ sthalaṃ kiṃ cid upetya ca krīḍāvasāne sarve te śucivastrāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ sarvakāmasamṛddhaṃ tad annaṃ bubhujire śanaiḥ
english: Reaching a certain spot of ground at Pramāṇakoṭi, at the end of their sports all of them, clad in clean garments and well-adorned, leisurely enjoyed food rich in every delight.

sanskrit: divasānte pariśrāntā vihṛtya ca kurūdvahāḥ vihārāvasatheṣv eva vīrā vāsam arocayan
english: At the day's end, those heroes — the upholders of the Kuru line — were thoroughly fatigued from their revels and were pleased to take their rest in the very pavilions of sport.

sanskrit: khinnas tu balavān bhīmo vyāyāmābhyadhikas tadā vāhayitvā kumārāṃs tāñ jalakrīḍāgatān vibhuḥ pramāṇakoṭyāṃ vāsārthī suṣvāpāruhya tat sthalam
english: But the powerful Bhīma, that lord, exceedingly exhausted from his exertions, having carried those princes who had come for water-sports, climbed up that ground at Pramāṇakoṭi wishing to sleep there and fell fast asleep.

sanskrit: śītaṃ vāsaṃ samāsādya śrānto madavimohitaḥ niśceṣṭaḥ pāṇḍavo rājan suṣvāpa mṛtakalpavat
english: Finding a cool resting place, weary and befuddled with intoxication, that Pāṇḍava lay motionless, O king, and slept as though dead.

sanskrit: tato baddhvā latāpāśair bhīmaṃ duryodhanaḥ śanaiḥ gambhīraṃ bhīmavegaṃ ca sthalāj jalam apātayat
english: Then Duryodhana quietly bound Bhīma with bonds of creepers and hurled him — deep water and terrifying force notwithstanding — from the land into the river.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabuddhaḥ kaunteyaḥ sarvaṃ saṃchidya bandhanam udatiṣṭhaj jalād bhūyo bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then Bhīma, that foremost of strikers, the son of Kuntī, awoke, cut through all his bonds, and rose up out of the water.

sanskrit: suptaṃ cāpi punaḥ sarpais tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrair mahāviṣaiḥ kupitair daṃśayām āsa sarveṣv evāṅgamarmasu
english: Again, while he slept, Duryodhana had him bitten on every vital point of his body by enraged serpents with sharp fangs and terrible venom.

sanskrit: daṃṣṭrāś ca daṃṣṭriṇāṃ teṣāṃ marmasv api nipātitāḥ tvacaṃ naivāsya bibhiduḥ sāratvāt pṛthuvakṣasaḥ
english: Yet the fangs of those venomous creatures, though driven into his vital spots, could not pierce his skin, because of the hardness of that broad-chested man's body.

sanskrit: pratibuddhas tu bhīmas tān sarvān sarpān apothayat sārathiṃ cāsya dayitam apahastena jaghnivān
english: But when Bhīma awoke he beat down all those serpents and with the back of his hand struck down Duryodhana's beloved charioteer.

sanskrit: bhojane bhīmasenasya punaḥ prākṣepayad viṣam kālakūṭaṃ navaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ saṃbhṛtaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: Again Duryodhana introduced poison into Bhīmasena's food — fresh, potent kālakūṭa venom, collected and hair-raising in its power.

sanskrit: vaiśyāputras tadācaṣṭa pārthānāṃ hitakāmyayā tac cāpi bhuktvājarayad avikāro vṛkodaraḥ
english: A vaiśya's son informed the Pārthas of it out of desire for their welfare; yet even having eaten that, Vṛkodara digested it without any adverse effect.

sanskrit: vikāraṃ na hy ajanayat sutīkṣṇam api tad viṣam bhīmasaṃhanano bhīmas tad apy ajarayat tataḥ
english: For that poison, however intensely sharp, produced no disorder in him; Bhīma, of terrible bodily constitution, digested even that.

sanskrit: evaṃ duryodhanaḥ karṇaḥ śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ anekair abhyupāyais tāñ jighāṃsanti sma pāṇḍavān
english: Thus Duryodhana, Karṇa, and Śakuni son of Subala sought to kill the Pāṇḍavas by many stratagems.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś cāpi tat sarvaṃ pratyajānann ariṃdamāḥ udbhāvanam akurvanto vidurasya mate sthitāḥ
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, those tamers of enemies, were fully aware of all that, yet made no show of it, abiding by Vidura's counsel.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kṛpasyāpi mahābrahman saṃbhavaṃ vaktum arhasi śarastambhāt kathaṃ jajñe kathaṃ cāstrāṇy avāptavān
english: Janamejaya said: O great brāhmaṇa, you should also tell the birth of Kṛpa — how was he born from a clump of reeds, and how did he obtain mastery of weapons?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca maharṣer gautamasyāsīc charadvān nāma nāmataḥ putraḥ kila mahārāja jātaḥ saha śarair vibho
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: O great king, the great sage Gautama had a son named Śaradvān — born, it is said, together with arrows, O lord.

sanskrit: na tasya vedādhyayane tathā buddhir ajāyata yathāsya buddhir abhavad dhanurvede paraṃtapa
english: His mind did not incline to the study of the Vedas as it inclined toward the science of archery, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: adhijagmur yathā vedāṃs tapasā brahmavādinaḥ tathā sa tapasopetaḥ sarvāṇy astrāṇy avāpa ha
english: Just as the speakers of Brahman master the Vedas through austerity, so he, endowed with austerity, mastered all weapons.

sanskrit: dhanurvedaparatvāc ca tapasā vipulena ca bhṛśaṃ saṃtāpayām āsa devarājaṃ sa gautamaḥ
english: Through his supreme devotion to the science of archery and through his vast austerities, that Gautama greatly alarmed the king of the gods.

sanskrit: tato jālapadīṃ nāma devakanyāṃ sureśvaraḥ prāhiṇot tapaso vighnaṃ kuru tasyeti kaurava
english: Then the lord of the gods sent a celestial maiden named Jālapadī, saying "Create an obstacle to his austerity," O Kaurava.

sanskrit: sābhigamyāśramapadaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ śaradvataḥ dhanurbāṇadharaṃ bālā lobhayām āsa gautamam
english: She approached the charming hermitage of Śaradvat and that young woman, finding Gautama with bow and arrows in hand, enticed him with desire.

sanskrit: tām ekavasanāṃ dṛṣṭvā gautamo 'psarasaṃ vane loke 'pratimasaṃsthānām utphullanayano 'bhavat
english: Seeing that apsarā in the forest, clad in a single garment, of incomparable form in all the world, Gautama's eyes opened wide.

sanskrit: dhanuś ca hi śarāś cāsya karābhyāṃ prāpatan bhuvi vepathuś cāsya tāṃ dṛṣṭvā śarīre samajāyata
english: His bow and arrows fell from his hands to the ground, and seeing her a trembling arose in his body.

sanskrit: sa tu jñānagarīyastvāt tapasaś ca samanvayāt avatasthe mahāprājño dhairyeṇa parameṇa ha
english: But that great sage, by reason of the excellence of his knowledge and in consequence of his austerity, stood firm with the utmost steadiness.

sanskrit: yas tv asya sahasā rājan vikāraḥ samapadyata tena susrāva reto 'sya sa ca tan nāvabudhyata
english: Yet, O king, the agitation that suddenly overcame him caused his seed to flow out, and he did not perceive it.

sanskrit: sa vihāyāśramaṃ taṃ ca tāṃ caivāpsarasaṃ muniḥ jagāma retas tat tasya śarastambe papāta ha
english: That sage, abandoning both that hermitage and the apsarā, departed; and his seed fell upon a clump of reeds.

sanskrit: śarastambe ca patitaṃ dvidhā tad abhavan nṛpa tasyātha mithunaṃ jajñe gautamasya śaradvataḥ
english: Having fallen upon the clump of reeds it divided into two, O king, and from that was born a twin pair — the offspring of Gautama Śaradvat.

sanskrit: mṛgayāṃ carato rājñaḥ śaṃtanos tu yadṛcchayā kaś cit senācaro 'raṇye mithunaṃ tad apaśyata
english: While king Śaṃtanu was out on a hunt, a certain soldier of his army happened to see that twin pair in the forest.

sanskrit: dhanuś ca saśaraṃ dṛṣṭvā tathā kṛṣṇājināni ca vyavasya brāhmaṇāpatyaṃ dhanurvedāntagasya tat sa rājñe darśayām āsa mithunaṃ saśaraṃ tadā
english: Seeing the bow with arrows and the black antelope skins, and judging the twins to be the offspring of a brāhmaṇa fully versed in the science of archery, he brought and showed the armed twin pair to the king.
